   440  end Polynomial

   442  section generic
   443  
   444  /-!
   445  ### Mahler Measure on Other Rings
   446  
   447  While the Mahler measure is an inherently Complex concept, we often want to work with it for
   448  polynomials with coefficients in subrings of `ℂ`. To do so, we introduce `mapMahlerMeasure`. This
   449  takes a `RingHom A ℂ` which takes the polynomial from `A[X]` to `ℂ[X]`.
   450  
   451  Some lemmas require the `RingHom` to also preserve the norm on the base ring, e.g.,
   452  `leadingCoeff_le_mapMahlerMeasure`. Those will come below.
   453  -/
   454  
   455  namespace Polynomial
   456  
   457  variable {A : Type*} [Semiring A] (p : A[X]) (v : A →+* ℂ)
   458  
   459  /-- The Mahler measure for polynomials on rings other than `ℂ`. Most theorems
   460  will require `A` to be a `NormedRing` and `v` to be an isometry. See, e.g.,
   461  `mapMahlerMeasure_const` -/
   462  noncomputable def mapMahlerMeasure := (p.map v).mahlerMeasure
   463  
   464  lemma mapMahlerMeasure_eq : p.mapMahlerMeasure v = (p.map v).mahlerMeasure := rfl
   465  
   466  lemma mapMahlerMeasure_mul (f g : A[X]) :
   467      (f * g).mapMahlerMeasure v = (f.mapMahlerMeasure v) * (g.mapMahlerMeasure v) := by
   468    simp [mapMahlerMeasure, mahlerMeasure_mul]
   469  
   470  lemma mapMahlerMeasure_nonneg : 0 ≤ p.mapMahlerMeasure v :=
   471    Polynomial.mahlerMeasure_nonneg _
   472  
   473  @[simp]
   474  lemma mapMahlerMeasure_zero : (0 : A[X]).mapMahlerMeasure v = 0 := by
   475    simp [mapMahlerMeasure]
   476  
   477  @[simp]
   478  lemma mapMahlerMeasure_one : (1 : A[X]).mapMahlerMeasure v = 1 := by
   479    simp [mapMahlerMeasure]
   480  
   481  variable {A : Type*} [NormedRing A] (p : A[X]) (v : A →+* ℂ)
   482  
   483  lemma mapMahlerMeasure_const (hv : Isometry v) (z : A) : (C z).mapMahlerMeasure v = ‖z‖ := by
   484    simp [mapMahlerMeasure, hv.norm_map_of_map_zero (map_zero _)]
   485  
   486  lemma leadingCoeff_le_mapMahlerMeasure (hv : Isometry v) :
   487      ‖p.leadingCoeff‖ ≤ p.mapMahlerMeasure v := by
   488    by_cases hp : p.leadingCoeff = 0

   490    · have hv_ne : v p.leadingCoeff ≠ 0 :=
   491        fun h ↦ hp <| hv.injective <| h.trans (map_zero _).symm
   492      have hv_norm : ‖v p.leadingCoeff‖ = ‖p.leadingCoeff‖ := hv.norm_map_of_map_zero (map_zero _) _
   493      grw [← hv_norm, ← leadingCoeff_map_of_leadingCoeff_ne_zero v hv_ne,
   494        leadingCoeff_le_mahlerMeasure, mapMahlerMeasure]
   495

   498      1 ≤ p.mapMahlerMeasure v := by
   499    grw [← p.leadingCoeff_le_mapMahlerMeasure v hv, hp.leadingCoeff, norm_one]
